name: Nelson Carbone
life: “My first cart belonged to a sailor who made very weak coffee.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Nelson by a small Saturday habit. Nelson watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I sell coffee on the old corner. My first customer is now a pensioner who only comes to talk.
appearance: Nelson has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. In conversation Nelson turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Nelson carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To give the cart a new set of regulars without losing the old neighbor.
family: Samuel Molina is Nelson’s cousin. Nelson checks the date twice. Samuel brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *One clean day*, Samuel says, “I only knew my partner's working voice. I heard his school nickname and he sounded fourteen.”
connections: Teal Holmes. The empty coffee corner finally has an errand for the person who found the ring.

reactions.response: Nelson asks one rider from each corner to walk the new distance.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Nelson asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.
